title: bls12-381-g1-ecdlp: Cheon subgroup walk with fixed-base comb tables

claims.statement: For uniform s in Z_r^* (r the BLS12-381 scalar field order), given T=[s]P0 and A_i=[s^i]P0 for i=1..n with n=2^20, the algorithm in proof.md recovers s with probability at least 0.40 and is run under a hard work meter that halts when its total reaches 2^120.911517 target-group-operation equivalents at n=2^20, which includes preprocessing, the walk, distinguished-point storage and lookup in a bounded table, restarts, the square-root chain, verification and output, all at worst-case bounds. Work is W = H + R/C with C=2000, where H counts reference units (batched affine G1 additions and doublings, 16 per walk point and restart) and R counts all other scalar instructions: 1895.45 per walk point measured by Callgrind on blst, and analytic bounds for the remaining work (proof.md sections 3 and 5). The reduction takes h = s^(2^20) in the subgroup H of order (r-1)/2^20, solves [h]P0 = A_d by a distinguished-point tame/wild walk on H modulo mu6 = {+-1, +-lambda, +-lambda^2} with 64 multipliers in H, with 256 round-robin records and a fixed budget of S + 2^108 points (S = ceil(2 sqrt(13/20 * M)), the random-mapping budget), and recovers s from h by 20 square roots fixed by the public powers A_(2^j). Peak memory is at most 2^34.178981 bytes. Preprocessing is at most 2^22.840069 units. Nonuniform advice is 0 bytes. The success bound rests on the random-mapping heuristic H1 (proof.md section 4) and on analytic losses totalling 0.00196, charged in proof.md section 4. The claimed 0.40 is below the Wilson 95% lower bound (0.4227) of 4000 fresh toy trials at the claim budget, minus those losses; it is not a proof. This is a classical cold attack on one target, not a practical break.

experiments.purpose: Run the walk of proof.md on a generic prime-order group whose exponent is hidden behind keyed labels, with mu6 acting as an endomorphism, and recover s from T and the powers A_(2^j) through the full reduction and square-root chain. It checks correctness, counts walk steps to the first tame-wild collision and compares the empirical CDF with the random-mapping model. Toy scale only: it tests correctness and collision statistics, not the cost of a BLS12-381 step.
Recompute W(2^20) = H + R/C, time_log2, the success model, the trail and table sizes and the peak memory from the stated parameters, using exact integer arithmetic and the vendored exact.py.
